framework.name: Federal Reserve SR 11-7 Model Risk Management
framework.jurisdiction: United States — Banking and Financial Services
framework.description: Supervisory guidance establishing a comprehensive framework for model risk management in banking organisations. Requires robust model development and validation processes, independent model validation, sound governance and oversight, and ongoing monitoring. Applies to all models including AI/ML systems used in financial decisions, credit underwriting, fraud detection, market risk, and customer-facing applications.

requirements.title: MRM-1 — Model Inventory
requirements.text: Banking organisations shall maintain a comprehensive inventory of all models in use. The inventory shall include model identification, purpose, business owner, technical owner, deployment status, tier/risk rating, validation status, and last validation date. AI/ML systems are explicitly included in scope.

controls.description: Maintain a complete and current model inventory covering all quantitative models and AI/ML systems
Assign risk tiers to all models based on materiality, complexity, and potential impact
Track and report on validation status for each model in the inventory

requirements.title: MRM-2 — Model Development Documentation
requirements.text: Model development shall be documented comprehensively, including: purpose and intended use; theoretical basis and methodology; data used; assumptions and limitations; performance assessment; and development testing results. Documentation for AI/ML models shall additionally cover training data, feature engineering, hyperparameter tuning, and model selection rationale.
requirements.scope: All SR 11-7 regulated institutions — model developers

controls.description: Produce comprehensive technical documentation for each model covering methodology, data, assumptions, and limitations
For AI/ML models, document training data sources, preprocessing, feature selection, and model architecture decisions
Document model performance benchmarks and testing results from development

requirements.title: MRM-3 — Model Implementation Controls
requirements.text: Model implementation shall be controlled and documented. Implementation testing shall verify the model produces the intended results in the production environment. Change management processes shall govern model updates and retraining. AI/ML model deployment pipelines shall include automated testing gates.

controls.description: Conduct implementation testing to verify model behaves as designed in the production environment
Implement change management controls for model updates, retraining, and version changes
Maintain version control for AI/ML models including training code, model artefacts, and configurations

requirements.title: MRM-4 — Appropriate Model Use
requirements.text: Models shall be used only for their intended purposes and within their established limitations. Users of model outputs shall receive appropriate training and understand model constraints. Significant deviations from intended use shall trigger re-validation.
requirements.scope: All SR 11-7 regulated institutions — model users and business owners

controls.description: Document approved use cases and constraints for each model and communicate to users
Implement controls to detect and address use outside approved boundaries

requirements.title: MRM-5 — Challenger Models
requirements.text: For material models, challenger models or benchmarking analyses shall be maintained to provide an independent performance reference. Challenger models are particularly important for AI/ML systems where model opacity makes direct validation more challenging.
requirements.scope: Material models at SR 11-7 regulated institutions

controls.description: Maintain challenger models or benchmark analyses for material AI/ML models
Review champion/challenger performance regularly and document results

requirements.title: MRM-6 — Independent Model Validation
requirements.text: Model validation shall be conducted by personnel or a function independent from model development. Independence is essential — validators must be able to challenge model design and outputs without conflicts of interest. For AI/ML models, validation requires specialised expertise in machine learning, statistics, and the relevant business domain.

controls.description: Establish a model validation function structurally independent from model development
Ensure validation personnel have appropriate AI/ML expertise for the models they validate

requirements.title: MRM-7 — Validation Scope and Depth
requirements.text: Model validation shall include: conceptual soundness review; data quality and representativeness assessment; ongoing performance monitoring review; sensitivity analysis; benchmarking; and outcomes analysis. AI/ML validation additionally requires evaluation of: feature importance stability; model interpretability; distributional shift detection; and adversarial robustness.
requirements.scope: All SR 11-7 regulated institutions — model validation function

controls.description: Conduct validation covering conceptual soundness, data quality, performance, and sensitivity analysis
evidence_needed: Validation report with all required sections

controls.description: For AI/ML models, conduct extended validation covering interpretability, distributional shift, and adversarial robustness
Conduct outcomes analysis comparing model predictions to actual outcomes

requirements.title: MRM-8 — Validation Findings and Remediation
requirements.text: Validation findings shall be documented, tracked, and remediated in a timely manner. Findings are classified by severity. Material findings must be escalated to senior management. Models with unresolved material findings shall operate under formal limitations with senior management approval.

controls.description: Maintain a validation findings tracker with classification, ownership, target dates, and status
Formally approve continued use of models with unresolved material findings with documented compensating controls
evidence_needed: Senior management approval for limited-use models

requirements.title: MRM-9 — Validation Frequency
requirements.text: Models shall be validated on a periodic basis consistent with their risk tier. High-tier models shall be validated at least annually; material events (regulatory changes, performance deterioration, significant data changes) shall trigger ad hoc re-validation. AI/ML models with frequent retraining require a validation protocol for each material update.

controls.description: Establish and adhere to risk-based validation frequency schedules
Define triggers for event-driven re-validation and monitor for trigger events

requirements.title: MRM-10 — Model Risk Management Policy
requirements.text: A comprehensive model risk management policy shall be in place, approved by senior management or the board, and reviewed at least annually. The policy shall define the scope of models covered, risk tiering criteria, validation requirements, and governance structure.

controls.description: Maintain a board/senior management approved MRM policy reviewed annually
Ensure MRM policy explicitly addresses AI/ML models
evidence_needed: AI/ML specific sections of MRM policy

requirements.title: MRM-11 — Model Risk Governance
requirements.text: Effective governance of model risk requires senior management and board oversight, clear ownership, and a model risk reporting process. A model risk committee or equivalent governance structure shall oversee model risk across the enterprise.

controls.description: Establish a model risk committee or equivalent body with board/senior management representation
Provide regular model risk reporting to senior management and the board

requirements.title: MRM-12 — Ongoing Model Performance Monitoring
requirements.text: Models in production shall be subject to ongoing performance monitoring to detect deterioration, data drift, and changing conditions that may invalidate model assumptions. Monitoring results shall be reviewed regularly and trigger re-validation when thresholds are breached. AI/ML models require real-time or near-real-time monitoring due to dynamic data environments.
requirements.scope: All SR 11-7 regulated institutions — model operations and validation

controls.description: Implement ongoing monitoring for all production models covering performance, data drift, and concept drift
Define and enforce performance thresholds that trigger review or re-validation
Conduct periodic population stability analysis and statistical performance reviews

requirements.title: MRM-13 — Model Risk Reporting
requirements.text: Model risk exposures, validation findings, and monitoring results shall be reported to senior management and, where material, to the board. Reports shall include aggregate model risk assessments, key metrics, and emerging risks including those from AI/ML deployment.

controls.description: Produce regular model risk management reports for senior management covering key risk indicators
Report AI/ML specific risks including explainability limitations, bias incidents, and data quality issues
evidence_needed: AI/ML risk section in model risk reports

requirements.title: MRM-14 — Third-Party and Vendor Model Risk
requirements.text: Models sourced from third-party vendors are subject to SR 11-7 requirements. The institution remains responsible for model risk regardless of source. Vendor model due diligence, validation requirements, and ongoing monitoring must be applied. AI models from foundation model providers require specific vendor risk assessment processes.
requirements.scope: All SR 11-7 regulated institutions using third-party models

controls.description: Conduct due diligence on all third-party models and AI vendors before deployment
Include MRM requirements in vendor contracts and monitor vendor compliance
Apply proportionate validation to vendor-provided AI models, supplementing vendor documentation

requirements.title: MRM-15 — AI/ML Model Explainability and Fairness
requirements.text: AI/ML models used in credit, fraud, and other consequential decisions must meet explainability requirements sufficient to comply with consumer protection laws (ECOA, FCRA). Fair lending analysis shall be conducted for credit models. Model outputs used in adverse action decisions must generate compliant reason codes.
requirements.scope: SR 11-7 regulated institutions using AI/ML in consumer-facing decisions

controls.description: Implement explainability solutions for all AI/ML models used in adverse action decisions
Conduct fair lending/bias analysis for credit and consumer-decision models
Document model limitations affecting explainability and implement compensating controls
